name: P-ONE

intervals.label: proposed
intervals.quote: The Pacific Ocean Neutrino Experiment is a proposed large-volume neutrino telescope in the Northeast Pacific Ocean, off the coast of Vancouver Island, Canada.
intervals.note: Start is the submission date of the 2020 Nature Astronomy design paper; the collaboration's own official site still describes the full array as 'proposed' as of this session's access date (2026-09-17). Pathfinder/demonstrator hardware (STRAW, STRAW-b, P-ONE-1) has already been built and deployed, but is modelled on detector:p-one rather than as a realised-status interval here, since the overall multi-cubic-kilometre array remains at the proposal stage per the collaboration's own current wording.

physics_goals.value: Build a multi-cubic-kilometre neutrino telescope in the deep Pacific Ocean to detect high-energy astrophysical neutrinos

quantity.quote: An established ONC site, known as the Cascadia Basin, 2,660 m below sea level, provides an ideal environment for a large scale undersea neutrino telescope.

notes: No site record was created for P-ONE in this wave: no source fetched this session (official site, Nature Astronomy design paper, EPJC site-characterization paper, Ocean Networks Canada pages, Wikipedia) gives a numeric latitude/longitude for the Cascadia Basin deployment point, only qualitative descriptions ('Cascadia Basin, ~200 km off the coast of British Columbia/Vancouver Island, Canada', depth 2660 m). Per A17, a coordinate was not invented; detector:p-one's placements are therefore also left empty, with the same note.

Timeline per the collaboration's own pages/papers: STRAW pathfinder deployed Spring 2018, commissioning completed January 2019; STRAW-b under construction as of the 2021 paper with deployment then planned for 2020 (i.e. the 2021 paper's schedule predates its own writing, an internal inconsistency in that source, left unresolved); P-ONE Explorer deployment was planned for 2023-2024 in the 2020 design paper; the official site (accessed 2026-09-17) states 'In 2026, the first detection line of P-ONE will be deployed' and separately notes a completed 'wet test of P-ONE-1 in Vancouver's Granville Island' and 'Completed integration of first detector line P-ONE-1' as past milestones -- it is not possible to tell from the fetched text alone whether the first real detection line has already been deployed in the ocean as of the access date or is still upcoming later in 2026.
Derived fields (detector_ids, site_ids, result_ids, document_ids) are deliberately not written (v0.2 A1).

summary.plain: A proposed neutrino telescope planned for the deep Pacific Ocean off Canada's west coast, building on an undersea science network. Small pathfinder instruments have already been tested there; the full telescope is still being built up piece by piece.
summary.technical: Proposed multi-cubic-kilometre water-Cherenkov neutrino telescope for the Cascadia Basin (2660 m depth) on Ocean Networks Canada's NEPTUNE cabled infrastructure off Vancouver Island. Pathfinder instruments (STRAW, deployed Spring 2018; STRAW-b; P-ONE-1) have validated the deep-sea deployment and optical-background characterization; the full array remains at the proposal stage as of the collaboration's own current description.
